result: Nested PCR found no XMRV or MLV sequences in blood DNA from 186 UK CDC-defined CFS patients (beta-globin control amplified in all).
reason: Independent UK cohort, same PCR target, null result consistent with the refuted-XMRV finding.

result: Overnight PSG showed disturbed sleep in female CFS vs matched controls; a maximal exercise test did not worsen sleep, and about half of patients slept better after it.
reason: Same PSG measure; adds post-exercise condition and sleepiness subgroups; sample size not given.

result: Maximal exercise did not worsen overnight PSG sleep in CFS, so PEM is not explained by worsened sleep.
reason: Does not measure PEM onset, duration or recovery time; the sleep link is covered by neuro-sleep.

result: 43-channel qEEG in 61 Fukuda CFS women vs 80 controls separated groups with 72-83% retrospective accuracy (alpha and beta bands) and showed greater left fronto-temporo-parietal source current during cognitive tasks.
reason: Same qEEG spectral measure with single-centre classification accuracy, as the finding describes.

result: In 200 CFS vs 200 donors, B19 seroprevalence was similar (75% vs 78%) but anti-NS1 IgG was 41.5% vs 7% (OR 9.42) and serum B19 DNA was found in 11 patients vs 0 controls.
reason: Covered by the newer infection-parvovirus-b19 finding listed in the brief.

result: Multiplex plasma panel in female CFS vs controls: LT-alpha, IL-1a, IL-1b, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-12 raised; IL-8, IL-13, IL-15 lowered; TNF, IFN-gamma, IL-2, IL-10, IL-17, IL-23 unchanged; best AUC IL-5 0.84.
reason: Only IL-4 matches the meta-analysis; TNF and IL-2 not different and several meta-null cytokines differ, so not a replication.

result: Echocardiography in 53 CFS patients (mean age 31) found a small left ventricular chamber with low cardiac output in a considerable number, often with slender build.
reason: Same measure (LV size, cardiac output); uncontrolled and abstract truncated.

result: Spectral analysis of overnight PSG in 35 population-based CFS vs 40 controls showed lower delta power in slow-wave sleep and lower alpha, theta, sigma and beta power in stage 2, SWS and REM.
reason: Measures sleep EEG microstructure, not the latency/efficiency claim; adds the microstructure angle the detail mentions.

result: Sleep-stage spectral EEG power was reduced across several bands in 35 CFS vs 40 controls, with delta reduced in SWS but raised in stage 1 and REM.
reason: Spectral power differences, but in sleep EEG rather than waking qEEG, so extends rather than replicates.

result: In 84 CDC CFS patients, lower 24-h urinary free cortisol (in medication-free patients) and a flatter salivary diurnal profile (n=56) predicted poorer response to CBT (39% responders overall).
reason: No control group, so cannot replicate low cortisol; adds clinical correlate of cortisol level within patients.
